pool.name: World Cup 2026
pool.tagline: 48 nations. One trophy. Draft the tournament.
pool.description: Only players heading to the 2026 World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico. Build the eleven that lifts it.

_instructions.status: TEMPLATE - no players yet. Paste player objects into the empty 'players' array below and the pool becomes playable automatically. Nothing else needs changing.

playerFields.id: REQUIRED. Number. Must be unique WITHIN THIS FILE (it does not have to be unique across pools). The draft uses it to make sure the same player is never offered twice.
playerFields.name: REQUIRED. Shown on the auction stage exactly as written.
playerFields.position: REQUIRED. One of: GK, LB, CB, RB, LWB, RWB, CDM, CM, CAM, LM, RM, LW, RW, ST, CF. This decides which formation slot the player can be offered for.
playerFields.rating: REQUIRED. Number, roughly 60-99. This drives the starting price, the phase bands and the AI's valuation - it is the single most important field.
playerFields.nationality: REQUIRED for this pool. Shown as a flag next to the name on every card. Use the plain English country name, e.g. 'Argentina', 'England', 'South Korea'.
playerFields.club: Optional. Shown in exports and squad detail.
playerFields.group: Optional. Tournament group, e.g. 'A'. Ignored by the draft engine - it is there so the pool stays useful for group-based features later.
playerFields.team: Optional. National team / event squad, if it differs from 'nationality'.

_instructions.positionAdvice: The draft offers every slot of the chosen formation. Thin positions are what break a pool, so aim for depth at the SPECIFIC positions rather than a big total: the game needs roughly (number of participants x 2) players for each position in the formation. Goalkeepers and full-backs are the ones people forget.
howToAddPlayers: 2. Paste it inside the empty 'players' array below.
3. Change the values. Give every player a different 'id'.
4. Separate players with commas. Save, reload the game, pick World Cup 2026 in any mode.
